E.Gordon proposed that F.G.Thomson should be President for the ensuing year. He said that Mr.Thomson had joined the Club in 1889 - two years after formation - and had been honoured with Life Membership as far back as 1897.
With all this immensity of Club work which he carried, Harry yet had time to win a Club Championship and to score in our winning Walking Championship teams. In 1924 FRANK THOMSON became Hon.
Amongst his colleagues were other legendary names such as Oscar Horwood, Harry Parker, Bob Ricketts, Frank Thomson, Jock McKay and Wally Bayliss.
Incidentally the first Belgravian to finish holds the Frank Thomson Trophy for a year. Frank was a Past President of the Club and the R.W.A.

…elgrave Harrier with its highest office for the ensuing year, thus carrying on a tradition of previous Belgravians like Frank Thomson, Alf Harley, Syd Roberts, John Goswell who held this high office.…
